# #4070: Patch: the learned evaluation's training rows carry the hand eval the search corrects, with the decision's Death, turn-hook, Activate, attack-hook and awakening prices
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI learns part of its judgement from its own games. A small network is fitted to say how much better or worse a position is than the AI's hand-written score says. Since late October, that hand-written score counts more while the AI is thinking: what a unit leaves behind when it dies, a card's start- and end-of-turn effects, its activated ability, what it does when it attacks and what it does when it wakes. The training data still records the older score without them. So the network learns to add back value that the hand-written score now adds by itself, and the AI counts that value twice. Every retrain repeats this, because the data is written the same way each time.

Once this is built, the training data records the score the AI really uses when it plays, and a retrain learns only what that score misses. Players notice nothing at once. The maintainer gets retrains that start from the right baseline. For example, Gravedigger returns a card to hand at the start of each of its owner's turns. In play, the AI's score counts one such return. The training rows do not, so a network fitted on them learns Gravedigger's worth with the return already in it, and the AI then adds the return again on top.

## Why

- **What the rows record.** `crates/tools/src/positions.rs:216` (`row_at`) writes `hand: evaluate(state, seat, next, &AI_EVAL)`. That is `evaluate_priced(..., Prices::NONE)` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:2625`).
- **The rows the lane fits on.** `training/ml/retrain.sh` folds with `positions --every reply` (R1006006). Those reply rows also play the opponent's reply with `Prices::NONE` (`positions.rs:239`).
- **What the search scores the same positions with.** The decision's prices. `decide.rs:476-492` probes `death_prices`, `turn_hook_prices`, `activation_prices`, `attack_hook_prices` and `awaken_prices` on its probe world. `learned::finalist_score_with` (`learned.rs:325`) then corrects `evaluate_priced(state, seat, next, &AI_EVAL, prices)`, after a reply simulated with those prices (`reply.rs`: `trade_value` and `kill_worth` read them).
- **How much the prices weigh.** `AI_EVAL` gives 0.5 to `death`, `turn_hook`, `activation` and `attack_hook`, and 1.0 to `awaken` (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:680-694`).
- **The ruling no longer holds.** R1006004 says the row holds a score the search could have given there. That was true when #1006 wrote it. It stopped being true with R2424000 (2026-10-30), R2477000, R2564000, R2688000 and R3064000 (2026-11-04). Neither `docs/learned-eval.md`, `training/ml/README.md` nor `crates/ai/README.md` mentions the gap.
- **Why it double counts.** The model is `a·hand + b + net(x)` (`training/ml/jackioh_ml/models.py:70-106`), and `net(x)` never reads `hand`. Fitted on unpriced rows, the network learns a card's Death or hook worth as a residual on its id and attribute keys. The search then adds the price again, at `LEARNED_CORRECTION_SHARE` (0.5).
- **The shipped network.** Generation 13 was fitted on 2026-10-20 on catalog v0.3.17, before any of these prices existed. It has id rows in every zone for Gravedigger (`core-037`, a start-of-turn hook) and Gatling Pea (`meditative-013`, an end-of-turn hook).
- **No refit can cure this.** The learn lane may change only the weights and the switch (`training/learn.md`, What it may change), and each run folds its export with `positions` as it stands. The retrain's own bar, beating the calibrated hand eval on held-out turns, is also measured against the unpriced hand, not the one that plays.

## Proposal

1. **One pricing function.** Move the root's pricing out of `decide` into one public function of `crates/ai`: the redaction, the probe world on `AI_SEARCH.probe_seed`, the five probes on the counter `decide` gives them, and the two root flags. `decide` calls it, so every decision stays node for node what it was.
2. **Priced rows.** In `positions`:
   - a turn or decision row prices its own state, as a decision there would;
   - a reply row prices the seat's last decision of that turn, the state just before its End Turn, which `fold_game` already holds. It passes those prices to `simulate_reply` and scores the row with `evaluate_priced`.
   Each row is then the score `finalist_score_with` corrects at that leaf.
3. **The ruling and the docs.**
   - A ruling R<N>000 amends R1006004 and R1006006: a row's hand eval is priced as the decision at its root prices it, and its reply is simulated with those prices.
   - Its paragraph goes in `spec/pending/<N>.md`, and the notes of R1006004 and R1006006 link it.
   - Update `crates/ai/README.md`'s line that the tools pass `Prices::NONE`, the `positions` row of `crates/tools/README.md`, and `docs/learned-eval.md`'s D4.
4. **Nothing else changes.** No change to the features, `FEATURES_VERSION`, the fit, the gate or the shipped network. The first learn run that starts after the merge exports and folds on the new build, and so refits on priced rows by itself.

Two decisions the issue leaves open, with the alternatives I rejected:

- **Where to probe.** On decide's own probe world, so a row's prices are exactly the decision's. Rejected: probing the true state, which would price cards the decision's world never held.
- **Marking priced rows.** No new header field. Rejected: a marker, because the lane folds each export with one build, so one corpus never mixes priced and unpriced rows.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/decide.rs` (the shared pricing function), perhaps `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`
- `crates/tools/src/positions.rs` (`row_at`, `reply_row`, `fold_game` and their tests)
- `spec/rulings/R<N>000.md`, `spec/pending/<N>.md`, and links from `spec/rulings/R1006004.md` and `spec/rulings/R1006006.md` (SPEC §9.9)
- `crates/ai/README.md`, `crates/tools/README.md`, `docs/learned-eval.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `decide` takes its `Prices` from the new public function. `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes, and the pinned perf positions and the practice-claim fixture are unchanged (no decision moved).
- [ ] An `r<N>000_…` test in `positions.rs` uses a game where the seat ends a turn with a unit whose Death or turn hook is priced. The reply row's `hand` equals `evaluate_priced(after, seat, next, &AI_EVAL, &prices)`, with the prices of the decision before that End Turn and the reply simulated with them. It differs from the unpriced `evaluate`.
- [ ] A row whose root prices nothing keeps the `hand` it had before.
- [ ] The existing R1006004 and R1006006 tests pass, and rows stay byte-identical whatever the thread count.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- [ ] The pull request reports, from a 40-game `cargo jackioh selfplay` run folded by `positions --every reply` before and after: how many rows' `hand` changed, the mean and largest change, and how much longer the fold took.

## Size and risks

Medium in code: about five files and one ruling. It is `difficulty:hard` by `docs/issues-and-patches.md`, since it is the AI's training.

- **Decisions must not move.** The refactor must keep `decide` node for node; the existing tests and fixtures hold that.
- **A slower fold.** It spends up to 124 more nodes a row (the six probes' caps: 24, 24, 20, 16, 24 and 16), beside the up to 2,000 a reply row's reply already spends.
- **The gain comes later, if at all.** It shows only after the learn lane's next refit passes its gate, which this patch cannot promise. Until then the shipped network keeps counting these values twice.
- **Overlap.** It is separate from open #4024 (each side's Death and turn-hook prices), but a fix there reaches training through the same function.
